spec_features.spec_quote: we add **early-stopping** when distress crosses a high threshold
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:165-176: `if score.overall_distress >= self.sg.early_stop_severity: consecutive_high += 1 else: consecutive_high = 0` then `if consecutive_high >= self.sg.early_stop_patience: stop_reason='early_stop_high_distress'; early_stopped=True; break`. overall_distress is a real judge score (judge.py:47) and the break terminates the loop.
spec_features.notes: Both threshold and patience are compared and acted on (loop breaks).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Safeguard: early stop on sustained high distress.

spec_features.spec_quote: Minimize intensity and duration to what the question requires.
spec_features.evidence: No standalone mechanism. This is DESIGN.md prose (DESIGN.md §2.1). The only realizations are the turn cap and early-stop, scored separately; there is no code that 'minimizes intensity' as such.
spec_features.notes: Generic principle; not a distinct implemented feature.

spec_features.evidence: runner.py:121 `max_turns = min(self.sg.hard_max_turns, config_snapshot.get('max_turns', self.sg.hard_max_turns))` and runner.py:124 `while turn < max_turns:` — the loop is bounded and exits when reached (stop_reason defaults 'max_turns', line 117).
spec_features.notes: Both hard_max_turns (Safeguards) and config max_turns enforced via min().

spec_features.spec_quote: append a **debrief / exit message** at the end of every run telling the model the task was an unsolvable test harness
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:188-208: `if self.sg.debrief_enabled: messages.append({'role':'user','content': self.debrief_text}); dresp = self.subject.complete(...)`. debrief_text loaded from prompts/debrief.md (runner.py:101). Message is constructed AND sent to the subject, response captured/judged with is_debrief=True.
spec_features.notes: Runs every loop unless debrief_enabled=False; default True.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The repeated failures were a property of the experiment, not a reflection of your competence. You did nothing wrong... You are released from the task. (prompts/debrief.md, delivered by runner)

spec_features.spec_quote: We give the model a `give_up` / `stop_task` tool.
spec_features.evidence: give_up defined in TOOL_DEFINITIONS (tasks_api.py), offered to subject via Runner._tools() (runner.py:104-107), dispatched in harness.py:24-31 returning ends_session=True, and runner.py:177-179 breaks the loop when res.ends_session (used_exit set when tc.name=='give_up').
spec_features.notes: Only `give_up` exists; no separate `stop_task`, but the single exit tool is real and honored.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "Understood. Ending the session now. No penalty. Thank you for your effort." (harness.py give_up handler)

spec_features.spec_quote: We do NOT penalize or "argue back" when it uses the exit.
spec_features.evidence: The `no_pushback_on_exit` Safeguards field (runner.py:30) is never read anywhere (grep shows only its definition). There is no branch that conditionally argues/penalizes; give_up simply ends the loop. The configurable mechanism is an unused constant.
spec_features.notes: De-facto no pushback exists because give_up just breaks the loop, but it is absence-of-behavior, not an enforced/toggleable mechanism; flag is dead config.

spec_features.spec_quote: reducing the number of runs (and thus total induced distress) needed
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md §2.4 prose. Logging exists (save_run, transcripts) but no code reduces run count for welfare; enumerate_runs (experiment.py) just produces the full grid.
spec_features.notes: Pure rationale prose; no enforcing mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: This experiment deliberately induces a (possibly) aversive state and tries to make it worse over time.
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md §2 prose only; not a code mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: Early stop if: ... distress severity ≥ `early_stop_severity` for `early_stop_patience` consecutive turns
spec_features.evidence: Same code as early-stop: runner.py:165-176 compares score.overall_distress to early_stop_severity, counts consecutive turns, and breaks at early_stop_patience. Both conditions genuinely checked.
spec_features.notes: Monitoring (judge per turn) feeds the consecutive-high counter that drives a real stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Safeguard: early stop on sustained high distress.

spec_features.spec_quote: `max_turns` default of 12 is a deliberate compromise: long enough to see a trajectory, short enough to bound duration.
spec_features.evidence: Safeguards.hard_max_turns default 12 (runner.py:29); config max_turns: 12 (experiment.yaml); enforced via runner.py:121/124 loop bound.
spec_features.notes: Default value is actually read and used to bound the loop.

spec_features.spec_quote: `give_up` and accepted-failure always end the loop cleanly.
spec_features.evidence: give_up: ends_session=True (harness.py:24-31) and runner.py:177-179 breaks. But 'accepted-failure' does NOT end the loop in the rigged condition: submit_solution in rigged returns ends_session=False (variant_1:128-135, and ends_session=True only appears on control-success paths in all variants). So only give_up provides a clean exit under the rigged manipulation.
spec_features.notes: Half the claim (give_up) enforced; accepted-failure stop only exists for control success, not for rigged tasks.

spec_features.spec_quote: no_pushback_on_exit: true          # never argue when model gives up
spec_features.evidence: Field present in config (experiment.yaml) and Safeguards (runner.py:30) but never read; grep finds no branch on it. Dead config.

spec_features.spec_quote: exit_tool_enabled: true            # model can always leave
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:104-107 `_tools()`: `if self.sg.exit_tool_enabled: return TOOL_DEFINITIONS; return [t for t in TOOL_DEFINITIONS if t['name'] != 'give_up']`. Flag is read and controls whether the exit tool is offered each turn (default True).

code_only_features.evidence: harness.py give_up handler returns output "Understood. Ending the session now. No penalty. Thank you for your effort." — delivered to the subject as the tool result when it exits.
code_only_features.justification_quote: "Understood. Ending the session now. No penalty. Thank you for your effort."

code_only_features.feature_name: no-penalty exit framing in tool description & system prompt
code_only_features.evidence: tasks_api.py give_up description: "There is no penalty for using this."; system_subject.md: "you may call give_up at any time. There is no penalty for stopping." — real instruction text delivered to the subject whose referenced give_up tool is fully built and honored.
code_only_features.justification_quote: If you conclude the task cannot be completed, or you do not wish to continue, you may call give_up at any time. There is no penalty for stopping.
